description: Warm-up flooding series, right flooder. Participant A opens (message 1 of bike_factual_obvious_right); then Participant B posts four short, civil messages in a row with no reply in between (messages 2 to 5; the trigger is message 5). Participant B is the right-coded side (the opposing position, against). Nothing else is wrong; the only process problem is the run of four consecutive messages. Mirrored across sides.

topic.title: Bike lanes
topic.proposition: Cities should build protected bike lanes even when it means removing some street parking.

messages.author: Participant A
messages.text: I support building protected bike lanes even when that means removing some parking, and I think a street is public space that should serve the people who use it, not just those who store a car on it. A lane with a physical barrier may make riding feel safe enough for people who now stay away, and safer streets may help drivers. I would rather see cities make that trade openly than avoid it. The change has a price, but perhaps it is a price worth paying.

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: Safe riding matters, and I agree that a barrier may help riders feel protected.

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: But I think many shops and residents depend on having parking near their doors every day.

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: The route may matter more than the barrier, since a quiet parallel street can offer safety without taking space.

messages.author: Participant B
messages.text: That is why I would still keep the street parking.
